inconsistencies: #34533 and #36330 address the same problem (periodic wallet rebroadcast leaking transaction origin when -privatebroadcast is set) with opposite approaches: route rebroadcasts through private broadcast vs. suppress resubmission entirely. They cannot both land as-is; #36330 is labelled [NO MERGE], so review #34533 first and use #36330 as the counter-proposal.

#36277 states it is an alternative to #34707 (complete all initial private-broadcast connections vs. retain finished broadcasts in memory for observability). Decide #36277 first; #34707 also carries a concept NACK on scope.
Chain: #36371 is stacked on #36369 and depends on its fixes and base test updates. Review #36369 first.
Chain: #35558 (P2, prefill) is stacked on #35724 (logging split-out). #35724 was promoted for exactly this reason and should be reviewed first despite being logging-only.
#36358 is a 31.x backport of #36312, which is not in this list. The backport should not be merged ahead of the master change; its priority mirrors the master PR.

Private-broadcast work forms a large cluster (#34322, #34533, #34707, #34271, #36277, #36330, #36358, #36429) touching overlapping state and all following merged #29415. They conflict with each other and are best sequenced in one pass rather than reviewed independently.

Refactor cluster all editing net_processing.cpp/net.cpp (#30988, #34565, #34824, #35040, #35315, #35502, #35522, #35561) will conflict heavily; ordering among them matters more than any individual one's merit. #34824 goes first since it removes a real recursive-mutex hazard.

#35888 and #35936 are both message-size validation hardening by the same author on different paths (outbound push vs. inbound locator deserialization); they are complementary, not duplicates, but should be reviewed together for a consistent limit-violation convention.
#33663 and #36208 both change AddrMan selection/freshness semantics and should be checked for interaction when the second is reviewed.
result.notes: The P2 band is large (23) because this category genuinely contains many independent privacy-leak, relay-liveness and DoS fixes of comparable consequence; P1 is reserved for the two memory-safety issues (remote orphanage memory exhaustion, out-of-bounds write in outbound message encoding). Private-broadcast follow-ups and net_processing refactors are the two clusters where review order matters more than individual band.
